sections.title: Outer measures, extension theorems and uniqueness of measures

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-measure-extension-C008 (partial): The construction or argument owed under proved=annex:p15.stieltjes-construction is not written out in full. The endpoint-limit step proves only the lower end, that inf F is the limit at minus infinity. The upper end is dismissed with 'The upper-end proof is the reversed argument' (handbook/annex/p15/measure-extension.tex line 296), which is a 'similarly' in place of written steps. That upper-end fact, F(infinity) = sup F as the limit at plus infinity including the infinite case, is needed later for targets with right endpoint infinity (annex lines 383-385). Second, the stated conclusion 'Its values on bounded intervals are finite' (body handbook/parts/p15/measure-extension.tex lines 211-212) is never proved for bounded intervals other than the finite-endpoint members I(a,b). The monotonicity step from containment in some (-n,n] is not written (annex lines 401-411).

ED26-P15-CH-measure-extension-C012 (partial): The construction or argument owed under proved=annex:p15.cdf-existence depends on an unstated assumption. The theorem concludes that the law of Q_F equals mu_F and that it is the unique Borel probability law with cumulative function F (body lines 297-299). For this the proof (handbook/annex/p15/measure-extension.tex lines 512-516) cites thm:p15-cdf-laws. That theorem's statement covers only two real random variables (handbook/parts/p15/measurable-probability.tex lines 443-444), and the handbook defines a CDF only for a real random variable (lines 417-425). mu_F, and any Borel probability measure with the same ray values, is never shown to be the law of a real random variable, for example the identity map on (R, B(R), mu_F). No direct argument on the ray pi-system or via the Stieltjes uniqueness clause is written either. So the equality-of-laws and uniqueness conclusions lack a written step.

sections.title: Lebesgue–Stieltjes measures and the construction of distributions

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-measure-extension-C008 (partial): The 'construction or argument' and the 'full treatment promised by its declared status' (proved=annex:p15.stieltjes-construction) are not fully supplied. In handbook/annex/p15/measure-extension.tex, the endpoint-limit step (lines 288-296) writes only the lower end (inf F is the limit at minus infinity). It disposes of the upper end with 'The upper-end proof is the reversed argument' (line 296), which is a 'similarly'-type elision. The unwritten upper-end fact is that F(n) increases to F(inf)=sup F, including when sup F is infinite. The proof uses it at lines 383-385 and 387-391 to truncate targets with b = infinity. So the following all depend on a step that is not written: the countable covering bound for unbounded targets (395-399), the second partition condition, the premeasure, existence of mu_F with mu_F(I(a,inf))=F(inf)-F(a), and mu_F(R)=F(inf)-F(-inf) (401-407). C008 becomes covered once the upper-end case is written out.

sections.title: Product sigma-algebras, product measures, Tonelli and Fubini

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-product-measures-C013 (partial): The full treatment promised by the declared status proved=annex:p15.absolute-iterated-series is not supplied. The series half of the proof connects the corollary's sums to Fubini's integrals only through two bare assertions. The first is 'The assumed sum is the first iterated absolute integral, because integration with respect to kappa is summation' (handbook/annex/p15/product-measures.tex 514-515). The second is 'counting-measure integration of that integrable section equals the sum' (519-521). Neither identity is derived in this proof or established anywhere on the route: the integral against counting measure on N+ of a nonnegative g equals the sum of g(n), and the signed version holds for an absolutely summable section. The closest result, thm:p15-expectation-law-integral (handbook/parts/p15/integration-expectation.tex 324-348), gives the sum formula only for countable atomic probability spaces. Three identifications are therefore unwritten: the hypothesis sum of the integrals of |f_n| with Fubini's premise, H with the section absolute integral (516-518), and S with Fubini's second section-integral function (522-523). All other parts of C013 (the Tonelli criterion at 499-504, product measurability of F, the absolute-convergence bound, integrability of each f_n) are written.
